conclusions: The native and preceding Python assignment search produce the same strict-improvement sequence in 256 completed small cases; both match independent exhaustive minima.
The four selected historical/current atom-set fragment pairs have identical weights, saved witness and anchors.
Removing only accepted edges did not reproduce the large slowdown; broadening domains alone also remained fast with accepted edges retained.
Broadening domains and removing accepted edges together reproduced five-second searches in all four selected fragments under the same native optimizer.
The historical Python optimizer also exhausted its allowance on the new broad fragments, so this observed failure mechanism does not require the C++ port.
Native execution is faster on identical constrained examples. Wall-limited search can still find a different incumbent because execution speed changes progress within its allowance.
The representation refactor broadened possible starting correspondences; this is a scientific behavior change, not merely set deduplication or a native execution port.
One selected 869 reverse fragment improved from ten events in the historical constrained relation to six in the broad relation; no exact decoded-output equivalence is claimed.
Both benchmark configurations use minimum + 5; expensive starting-map preparation occurs before the final window can filter contexts.
No complete ten-seed decoding result or repair acceptance follows from this diagnostic.
